premises: Grain refinement and uniform dispersion of hard intermetallic precipitates can be achieved by microalloying (e.g., with boron) or heat treatment in HEAs.
Such a refined and uniformly precipitated microstructure increases hardness and decreases plastic deformation.
This microstructural state stabilizes a coherent passive oxide film, minimizing defects.
A stable, coherent passive film impedes chloride ion penetration and corrosion.
The harder, refined microstructure resists mechanical wear, leading to simultaneous improvement in wear and corrosion resistance.
